channel.title: Valuation on Best of AI
channel.description: Recent content in Valuation on Best of AI

item.title: Buildium
item.description:
Buildium is designed for landlords and property managers who run a few dozen to a few thousand units. A manager can list vacancies, screen applicants, sign leases online, collect rent through a resident portal, and track maintenance requests with vendors. Owners can receive statements and reports, and community associations have their own tools.

Accounting is built in, with trust accounting, bank reconciliation, and tax reports that property managers need. Mobile apps let staff handle requests in the field. Some AI features help with tasks such as drafting messages and summarizing information, and integrations connect with listing sites, screening services, and other software.

item.title: HomeGauge
item.description:
HomeGauge is software for the home inspection trade. Inspectors collect findings on-site, add photos, and generate reports with standard language, ratings, and summaries for buyers and agents. Repair estimate features give clients an idea of costs.

The product has been around for years and has a loyal user base, along with scheduling and business tools. Newer rivals emphasize modern interfaces and automation, and AI features that draft report language.

HomeGauge is sold by subscription or license. Inspectors remain responsible for accuracy and compliance with standards of practice. Alternatives include Spectora, ISN, Horizon, Palmetto, and ITB. HomeGauge suits home inspectors.

item.title: Virtual Staging AI
item.description:
Virtual Staging AI is built for property listings. An agent uploads a photo of an empty room, selects a room type and style, and the AI places furniture and decor that fits the space. Results arrive in minutes, so listings can show potential before a sale.

Staged photos tend to attract more interest, and virtual staging costs far less than renting furniture. Many markets and listing services require disclosure that images are digitally staged, and the room must not be misrepresented.

item.title: Yardi
item.description:
Yardi is one of the largest suppliers of software to the real estate industry. Property managers use it to market units, screen applicants, sign leases, collect rent, track maintenance, and run accounting. Different products fit different segments: Voyager serves larger portfolios, Breeze suits smaller operators, and other tools cover commercial space, senior living, and investment management.

AI features are collected under Virtuoso, which Yardi uses for tasks like answering resident questions, drafting leasing responses, handling invoices and documents, and analyzing performance. The goal is to take routine work off property staff and to provide insights from data that the company already holds in its accounting and leasing systems.

item.title: AppFolio
item.description:
AppFolio runs the daily operations of a property management business. Staff list vacancies on rental sites, screen applicants, sign leases, collect rent online, and track maintenance requests and vendors. Owners receive statements and reports, and residents use a portal and app to pay and submit requests.

AI features take over routine communication. An assistant answers common tenant questions by text at any hour, qualifies leads, schedules showings, and flags maintenance requests that need attention. Analytics help managers see trends in occupancy, delinquency, and costs, and accounting tools are designed for property trust accounting.

item.title: BoxBrownie
item.description:
BoxBrownie serves real estate marketing. Agents and photographers upload listing photos, and editors, supported by AI, enhance the images by fixing exposure, correcting color, replacing dull skies, and removing clutter or distractions. Turnaround is typically quick, which suits fast-moving listings.

Virtual staging is a major product. The service places digital furniture and decor into photos of empty rooms so buyers can imagine the space, which costs far less than physical staging. Other services include twilight conversions, lawn improvements, and floor plans.

item.title: Zumper
item.description:
Zumper lists rentals with photos, prices, and neighborhood details. Renters filter by price, bedrooms, pets, and commute, save searches, and message landlords. A universal application and tools for screening speed up the process.

Recommendations use preferences and behavior, and data on rents helps renters understand local prices. Landlords and property managers pay to list and get leads.

Zumper is free for renters. Listings can be outdated, and renters should watch for scams. Alternatives include Zillow Rentals, Apartments.com, Rent.com, Trulia, and Craigslist. Zumper suits renters in major US cities.

item.title: Compass
item.description:
Compass is a brokerage that positions itself as a technology company. Its agents use a platform that combines a customer relationship manager, marketing tools for listings, market data, and transaction management in one place. Homebuyers and sellers use the site and app to search listings, see market trends, and work with an agent, and the tools are free to consumers because the company earns money through commissions on sales.

Technology supports the agent workflow. The platform helps with pricing recommendations, creates marketing materials such as brochures and social posts, tracks leads and client conversations, and organizes documents and deadlines through a deal. AI features assist with drafting listing descriptions, summarizing client interactions, and surfacing homes or clients to contact. The company has also tested private listings strategies for sellers.

item.title: Opendoor
item.description:
Opendoor popularized the iBuyer model. A homeowner enters an address and details, receives an offer within days based on the company’s pricing model and an inspection, and can close on a timeline they choose. The company then repairs and resells the home. The process appeals to sellers who value speed and certainty over getting the highest price.

Technology is central to the business. Machine learning models estimate what a home is worth and how long it will take to sell, using data on the property and the local market, and these estimates determine offers and risk. Opendoor also offers listing options for sellers who prefer to sell traditionally, along with buyer services such as touring homes with self-guided access in some markets.

item.title: Redfin
item.description:
Redfin helped modernize home search. Its site and app show listings with details, photos, and maps, along with estimated home values, price history, and tools to compare neighborhoods. A key difference from traditional brokerages is that its agents are salaried employees instead of paid mostly on commission, and Redfin has competed on lower listing fees and a customer-focused model.

Technology plays a large role. Its valuation model, the Redfin Estimate, uses machine learning on recent sales and listing data to estimate home values, and tools offer alerts, tours scheduling, and offers online. AI features help with search and recommendations. Rocket Companies, the owner of Rocket Mortgage, acquired Redfin, bringing mortgage and agent services together under a combined offering, including financing incentives when buyers use both.

item.title: Zillow
item.description:
Zillow is where many people begin looking for a home. Listings for sale and rent appear on maps and lists with photos, price history, taxes, and school details, and users can filter by price, size, and features, save searches, and get alerts when matching homes appear. Agents and landlords pay to advertise or manage listings.

Its signature feature is the Zestimate, an automated estimate of a home’s value based on public records, market data, and a machine learning model. It is useful as a rough guide but can be off for individual homes, and sellers should not treat it as an appraisal. Zillow also offers mortgage and agent referral services, rental tools, and an AI-powered search that accepts natural language descriptions.

item.title: Matterport
item.description:
Matterport captures spaces in 3D. A camera or a phone scans a property, and the software stitches the data into a navigable model, a virtual tour where viewers can walk through rooms, take measurements, and view floor plans. Real estate agents use it to show listings, and others use it to document sites.

Beyond tours, the platform serves professional needs. Contractors document existing conditions, insurers record property states, and facility managers keep a digital record of buildings. AI helps generate floor plans, label rooms, and create other outputs from scans.
